messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty P1 fired for tenant=helios-analytics on dedicated-eu-2.

pagerduty-bot: PD-9876 - High p95 latency & elevated errors. p95=1.2s (baseline 80ms), error_rate=4.8% over last 5m. Impacting ~12% of tenant requests. Auto-escalation to L2 in 2m if not ACKed. Runbook: https://runbooks.redwood/dedicated/tenant-latency

sam: @pagerduty-bot acked. I'm taking lead. Looking at Grafana / cluster metrics now.

maya: thanks @sam. I see the burst queue depth rising and KV-cache fallback count spiking in the last 3m. Could be reserved pool saturation + cache thrash.

sam: quick checks:
```
$ kubectl -n infra get pods -l cluster=dedicated-eu-2 -o wide
NAME                                        READY   STATUS    CPU(%)   GPU(%)
ded-node-7                                  1/1     Running   98       100
ded-node-8                                  1/1     Running   95       99
ded-batcher-2                                1/1     Running   88       85
```
Looks like two nodes at full cap. KV-cache miss rate jumped ~3x. Attaching grafana: https://grafana.redwood/d/dedicated/helios-analytics?from=-15m

leo: If reserved pool can't scale fast enough, trigger reserved-burst. Runbook step: `rctl reserved add --tenant helios-analytics --count 2 --pool dedicated-eu-2` (requires L2 approve). @maya can you validate spot capacity in eu region?

maya: eu spot capacity currently available +2 GPUs per AZ. Approving auto-burst if sam triggers.

sam: executing now:
```
$ rctl reserved add --tenant helios-analytics --count 2 --pool dedicated-eu-2
Request submitted -> job 4821
Job 4821: provisioning 2 nodes (expected ~2m)
```

opsbot: Action log: reserved-burst requested by sam (job 4821). Routing fallback enabled for tenant helios-analytics -> model-variant fallback: v1.2-low-latency. (see /ops/actions/4821)

pagerduty-bot: Severity update: continued elevated latency after provision; auto-escalation triggered to L2 (leo) due to sustained p95 > 800ms for 4m. L2 notified.

leo: acked. I'll join. Planning to drain the hottest node and move requests to the two newly provisioned nodes once they come up. Sam — please keep the KV-cache trace IDs; I'll want to inspect the cache eviction pattern.

sam: attaching recent logs (tail):
```
[2026-03-14T12:19:02Z] tenant=helios-analytics req=tx-9a3 evict=kvcache key=prefix-uid-42
[2026-03-14T12:19:03Z] tenant=helios-analytics req=tx-9a4 backend=runtime queue_ms=430
[2026-03-14T12:19:05Z] tenant=helios-analytics req=tx-9a7 err=timeout model=long-seq
```
Also noting increased tail latencies correlated with several >=1024 token requests.

emily: Customer impact note: CS notified. Customer-facing summary: "Intermittent latency spikes for some long sequences affecting a subset (~12%) of requests. No data exposure. Engineering working on scaling and mitigation." Emily to escalate to account manager after we stabilize.

maya: provisioning shows two nodes healthy now. Sam, can you confirm traffic moved?

sam: new nodes registered and LB rebalanced. p95 dropping from 1.2s -> 360ms in last 90s, errors down to 1.1%. Continuing to watch.

opsbot: Observability note: KV-cache fallback rate decreasing after scale event. Auto-caching warmers queued (job 4822).

maya: handoff: @leo will take the night-oncall. Summary: PD-9876 fired for high p95 on dedicated-eu-2 for tenant helios-analytics. Cause: reserved pool saturation + KV-cache thrash on heavy long-sequence traffic. Actions taken: ack, rctl reserved add (+2 nodes), enabled model-variant fallback, warmed cache, drained hot node planned. Impact: ~12% tenant requests affected, higher latencies for long sequences, no security impact. Current state: p95 ~360ms, error_rate ~1.1%, monitoring.

leo: ack handoff. I'll run the follow-up: drain ded-node-7, inspect cache eviction traces, and keep PD incident open until 1h of stable p95 < 150ms or rollback actions completed. Will post next update in 15m.

incident-bot: PD-9876 status -> investigating. Owner: leo. Escalation path intact.

sam: thanks team. Leaving monitoring to @leo. Closing my loop. :thumbsup:
